ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Someone throws darts. He stands on the throwing line and horizontally throws multiple darts from the same point C. As a result, the dart thrown with initial velocity vA hits point A, and the dart thrown with initial velocity vB hits point B, and it never hits the center O of the vertical target, as shown in Figure 14. In order to make the dart hit the center O of the target, the adjustment he may make is (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Keep the initial velocity vB unchanged, and raise the height of the throwing point C

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Someone horizontally throws darts from the same point C. The dart thrown with initial velocity vA hits point A, and the dart thrown with initial velocity vB hits point B, and it never hits the center O of the vertical target. If the initial velocity vB is kept unchanged, in order to make the dart hit the center O of the target, how should the throwing point C be adjusted?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Keep the initial velocity vB unchanged, and raise the height of the throwing point C
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the throwing point C is on the left, and the vertical target is on the right; the center of the target is marked as O, A is located above O, and B is located below O. In the schematic on the left, the trajectory of the dart horizontally thrown from C bends to the right and downward; according to the problem statement, currently when the initial velocity vB is used, the dart hits the lower point B. Then reason: Keep the initial velocity vB unchanged, and the horizontal distance to the target surface unchanged, then the flight time t=x/vB for the dart to reach the target surface is unchanged, and the amount of fall caused by gravity, 1/2gt², is also unchanged. Therefore, the shape of the trajectory relative to the throwing point and the amount of fall are unchanged. To change the trajectory that originally landed at point B to land at point O above it, the entire trajectory can only be moved upward as a whole, so the height of the throwing point C should be raised.
